hook: Why is bubble sort the algorithm everyone learns and no one uses?

narration.text: Bubble sort repeatedly compares neighbors and swaps them when they're out of order.
Pass one: sweep left to right — swap when the left is bigger. The largest value bubbles to the end.
Pass two: the same sweep over what's left. Another big value settles into place.
The remaining passes finish the job, shrinking the unsorted region until nothing needs to swap.
Ten comparisons and six swaps for five elements. That's O(n squared) — much slower than binary search.

youtube.title: Bubble Sort in 30 Seconds
youtube.description: How bubble sort works: repeatedly compare and swap neighboring elements until the array is sorted. O(n²) time, O(1) space.
